_comment: Tier-2 for kratos::cable_net#2 — the uBLAS aliasing in EmpiricalSpringElement3D2N's GlobalizeVector. EXECUTED 2026-08-06 on this host with /usr/bin/python3 (Kratos 10.4 Release, GCC-14.2 build, CableNetApplication present; the repo .venv wheel cannot load here — its Kratos.so wants GLIBC_2.32 — so the runner needs KRATOS_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3). One two-node EmpiricalSpringElement3D2N with F(dl) = 1000*dl was stretched 0.01 purely along its own axis at five orientations, and CalculateRightHandSide / CalculateLeftHandSide read directly. Printed: force magnitude 1.000000e+01 (exact) with alignment 1.000000 for the x-aligned spring; EXACTLY 0.000000e+00 for the y-aligned and z-aligned springs; 8.660254e+00 at alignment 0.985599 for the (1,1,0) spring and 8.135728e+00 at alignment 0.413888 for the (1,1,1) spring, against an exact 1.000000e+01 in every case. The axial stiffness came back 1.000000e+03 — exact — at ALL five orientations, so the claim's 'the LHS is unaffected' is confirmed and this is the right-tangent/wrong-force pathology: Newton converges quadratically onto a wrong equilibrium and the iteration count never moves. Direction is checked by the signed cosine between the returned force and the element's own unit axis, not by a norm, because a norm cannot tell a rotated force from a correct one. MUTATION EVIDENCE: replacing probe() with a correctly globalised element (magnitude = k*dl, alignment = 1, stiffness = k at every orientation) made the fixture print y_aligned_spring_force_is_exactly_zero=False, z_aligned_spring_force_is_exactly_zero=False, xy_skew_force_is_misdirected=False, xyz_skew_force_is_misdirected=False and right_tangent_with_wrong_internal_force=False, emit five FAIL: lines, drop the _verified sentinel and return 2. KratosMultiphysics and CableNetApplication are imported at module scope, so with Kratos absent the process dies on the import and the runner records a failure, never a pass.
